precepts.text: Let your yeas be yea, and your nays be nay, and everything else is what? Everything else is evil.
precepts.point: Hey, Malachi, how many times you hear, brother, listen, brother, stop talking. Brother, stop talking. Oh, God. Brother, I'm trying to help you. Stop talking. Oh my goodness. You don't realise. You think you saying something deep, you're burying yourself. He just can't stop talking. Let your yeas be yea, and your nays be nay, and everything else is what? Nobody knows the scripture. What is it? Everything else is evil. The scripture says in a multitude of words there lacketh not, or wanteth not, sin. It means does not lack. You're over-explaining. Why does she have your phone? Well, okay, there you go. This is your senses being exercised.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Wanteth not means it does not lack: where there are many words, sin is never missing. Christ gave the rule for our speech: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” Let your yea be yea and your nay be nay, and everything else is evil.

How many times do you hear it: brother, listen, stop talking. Brother, I am trying to help you, stop talking. You think you are saying something deep, and you are burying yourself. He just cannot stop talking.

Take the brother at work who handed his phone to a girl while the other brother stepped to the back. Asked why, he said it was nothing. Then it was business. What business do you have with her, when we just walked into this place? Nah, it was nothing. Now you are repeating yourself. That is the multitude of words, the over-explaining, and it gave him away. Just by seeing the phone the other brother knew something was not right, and there was more behind it.

That is the ears and the eyes being exercised. Your ears have to be tuned to the subtleties in speech, and a man's face will tell you what is really going on, not what he says. The heart takes what it has seen and heard, processes it and comes to a conclusion; to discern between good and evil you have to be spiritual. Speech reveals the thoughts formed in the heart, so the one who refrains his lips and keeps his yea to yea and his nay to nay is wise.

precepts.text: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it. This is one of my favorite verses. When the Lord blesses you there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains. I will use it in the way of lifting weights. When you exercise or you lift weight, the muscles are being broken down. It is an acid that releases in your body and it breaks down those muscles. But when it regroups it builds more muscle and it makes you look stronger. And when you look stronger you feel stronger and you sit up a little bit more. Shout out to the greens men and the brothers that got necks. You know them brothers, they were fat and their neck sat like this, and then they start to slim down and now you can see that they have got a neck. You start to get praised, hey listen, bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed. That is what being around wise men does. And even the men that were walking with Christ, everybody knew who was walking with Christ. You sound like him. You talk like him. You have got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up. It makes you feel and be somebody, around wise men.
precepts.point: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise. So if you broaden that circle to wise men, meaning men that keep the commandments, then you will have righteous success.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
“He that walketh with wise men shall be wise”: broaden your circle to wise men, men that keep the commandments, and you'll have righteous success. Speaking of that: “The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.” When the Lord blesses you, there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains.

Think of lifting weights. When you exercise, the muscles are being broken down; an acid releases in your body and breaks them down. But when it regroups, it builds more muscle and makes you look stronger, and when you look stronger you feel stronger and sit up a little more. Shout out to the Greensmen and the brothers that got necks: they were fat and their neck sat down in their shoulders, then they slimmed down and now you can see they've got a neck. People start praising you: bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed.

That is what being around wise men does. Everybody knew the men who walked with Christ: you sound like him, you talk like him, you've got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up and makes you feel and be somebody.

Evil success is different. Some kids think making money on OnlyFans or social media content is success; it's not, and it's nothing to glory in. It seems good and brings profit, so it is “abomination to fools to depart from evil”. That's why rappers and entertainers keep selling digital crack and the prostitute lifestyle to the community but not to their own kids. Evil success comes with sorrow; the blessing of the Lord adds none.

precepts.text: He that uttereth a slander is a fool.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off”: God will cut you off, cut off from the book of the living. Proverbs shows what is really behind slander: “He that hideth hatred with lying lips, and he that uttereth a slander, is a fool.”

When somebody lies on you or slanders you, what that really says is that there is hatred there. The lying lips are hiding hatred.

“and he that uttereth a slander”: you had Tyre Gas, you had Lightfoot, you had these guys uttering slanders, and their followers talk that way because their leaders are the same way. They run with slander. As a leader you are supposed to hear an outrageous lie and say, I do not believe that. One woman said we came to Canada on a magic school bus, and some leaders believed it.

God says you are a fool to listen to lies, run with them and put them out there. Slander is defamation: running with an accusation without two or three witnesses, and God cuts that man off.

precepts.text: The wise in heart receive commandments; a prating fool shall fall.
precepts.point: So if you want to know whether you are wise, ask whether you are keeping the commandments, or whether you are a prating fool talking about the ex Jesus and hermeneutics.

precepts.text: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin.
precepts.point: Swear not at all, neither by heaven nor by the earth nor by Jerusalem nor by thy head. Let your communication be Yea, yea; Nay, nay.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Christ says, “Swear not at all”, not by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by Jerusalem, nor by thy head, “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

Solomon gives the reason: “In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.” Piling up oaths is a multitude of words, and where there is a multitude of words there is sin. The wise man refrains his lips and lets his yes be yes and his no be no.
